text: DSH Git Workbench 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的 Git 工作台，在会话侧边栏提供提交、历史和差异面板，并通过模型工具操作仓库。它支持查看状态与提交差异、按文件或区块或行暂存、提交变更、查看分支和 blame。适合希望在 DSH 对话界面内完成日常版本控制的开发者；需要本机安装 git。

DSH Git Workbench adds commit, history, and diff panels to the DSH web client. Review status and diffs, stage files or selected lines, commit changes, browse branches, and inspect line history. For developers managing Git from DSH; local git is required.

DSH Git Workbench 的功能「查看仓库状态」：在提交面板或模型工具中查看分支、上游领先落后情况，以及暂存、修改、未跟踪和冲突文件。
DSH Git Workbench 的功能「精细暂存」：选择整个文件、某个差异区块或区块内的行，将选中改动加入暂存区，也可按相同粒度取消暂存。
DSH Git Workbench 的功能「查看提交历史」：在历史面板浏览提交图、提交详情和文件列表，并可按作者、消息、分支等条件查找记录。
DSH Git Workbench 的功能「代码差异查看」：打开文件差异面板，以并排或统一视图检查修改，并查看区块和行级内容。

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_status：Show the Git working-tree status of a repository: current branch, upstream ahead/behind, and every staged, modified, untracked or conflicted file. Call this before staging or committing so you know what actually changed.
@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_diff：Show a unified diff with hunk boundaries. Use staged=true for index-vs-HEAD, omit it for worktree-vs-index. Pass file to limit the diff to one path.
@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_log：List recent commits across all refs (hash, author, date, subject, refs). Use it to find a commit before calling git_show.
@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_show：Show one commit: metadata, message and its full diff.

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_stage：Stage or unstage changes. mode=file moves the whole file, mode=hunk moves one hunk by index, mode=lines moves individual lines inside a hunk (0-based everywhere: the first hunk is 0, the first line of a hunk is 0).
@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_commit：Commit the staged index with a message. Use amend=true only when the user explicitly asks to rewrite the previous commit.
@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_branch：List branches/tags, or switch to an existing branch, or create one. Never forces a checkout over dirty changes.
@yann9/dsh-git-workbench 提供工具 git_blame：Annotate a file with the commit, author and date that last touched each line.

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · dsh-git-workbench：**A JetBrains-style Git workbench for DeepSeek Harness.** Local Changes tree, hunk- and line-level staging, side-by-side diff, commit window, commit graph, annotate, interactive rebase, shelve, three-way conflict resolution — all next to the conversation, no terminal switching.

> The goal is not "being able to commit", but seeing **which line changed, which hunk gets staged, and which branch the commit lands on** as clearly as in IDEA.

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · What it is：DSH's right sidebar is a draggable tab area, which maps to IDE tool windows; the diff opens in the main area like an editor tab and is a **singleton** — opening another file replaces the content instead of stacking tabs.

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · What it is：| JetBrains | Here | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Commit tool window | **Commit** tab | changes tree + changelists + conflicts + message + `AI` / `Recent` / `Checks` / `Amend` |
| Log tool window | **History** tab | commit graph + commit details + file list, read-only |
| Editor diff tab | **Diff** view (main area) | side-by-side / unified, hunk & line staging, annotate, conflict view |

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · What it is：Commit and history keep their own selection, scroll, filters and draft; the diff decides what it shows and whether it is writable from its `source` (`working` = writable, `commit` / `turn` = read-only).

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · What it is：It also plugs into DSH surfaces you already use: the branch chip in the session header, the branch picker in the new-session hero, the `Git` buttons on turn cards and the Files tab, and the change bar above the composer. The repository follows the session cwd — switching sessions switches repositories.

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · Configuration：Everything is editable in **Settings → Plugins → Git workbench**, or in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: git-workbench
      name: '@yann9/dsh-git-workbench'
      config:

Unwritten keys take the defaults above. `readOnly: true` turns the workbench into a read-only review panel: staging, committing, branches, the network and conflict resolution are all disabled, and the HTTP write endpoints return 403 (except `/config`).

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · Highlights：- **Staging** — whole file, hunk (cropped patch → `git apply --cached`), or individual lines; unstaging is equally precise. Commits always use the index.
- **Reading diffs** — side-by-side / unified, dual line numbers, word-level highlights, ignore-whitespace (read-only), context folding, `‹ n/m ›` file navigation and `F7` hunk navigation.
- **Committing** — `Ctrl+Enter`, AI draft, `↑` to recall previous messages, amend, changelists, and before-commit checks taken from the repo's own `package.json` scripts.
- **History** — DAG graph, sortable and resizable columns, group by branch/author/date, structured filters (`author:` `message:` `hash:` `tag:` `branch:` `date:`), multi-select for batch cherry-pick / revert.
- **Rewriting history** — interactive rebase (pick/squash/fixup/drop), reword, undo commit, cherry-pick, revert, soft/hard reset — all behind explicit confirmations.
- **Branches & remotes** — switch/create/rename, `↑N ↓N` ahead-behind badges, set/unset upstream, compare, rebase onto, fetch/pull/push (Pick a remote on first push), manage remotes.
- **Conflicts & sequencer** — separate unmerged group, three-way view with per-block

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · Keyboard shortcuts：| Action | Shortcut / gesture |
|---|---|
| Refresh | `F5` |
| Commit | `Ctrl/Cmd + Enter` |
| Focus the message box | `Ctrl/Cmd + K` |
| Draft the message with the model | `Ctrl/Cmd + G` |
| Previous / next file | `Alt + ↑` / `Alt + ↓`, or the `‹ n/m ›` in the diff header |
| Previous / next hunk | `Shift + F7` / `F7`, or the `↑ Hunk ↓` toolbar — walking off either end continues into the neighbouring file |
| Revert the current hunk | `Ctrl + Alt + R` (working-tree source, asks first) |
| Pick a file from the current set | click the `3 / 5` in the diff header |
| Back to the conversation from a diff | `Esc`, or the ✕ at the top right |
| Walk the history one commit at a time | `↑` / `↓`, `Home` / `End`; `Enter` or a double-click opens the diff |
| Multi-select commits | `Ctrl/⌘`-click, `Shift`-click for a range, `Ctrl+A` for everything visible, `Esc` to clear |
| Recall a previous message in an empty box | `↑` / `↓` |
| Stage selected lines | click the `+` / `−` at the line head to select, then **Stage selected lines** |

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · Development：```bash
npm test                     # 137 tests against real git repositories

node scripts/dev-server.js <repo> 5178   # API only, no UI
```

No build step: host and client are plain ESM, so `link:` + restart is the whole loop. See [docs/development.md](docs/development.md).

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · Security：Every git call is `spawn('git', argv)` with **no shell**; writes are serialized; paths are validated against `..` and option injection; cross-origin requests are rejected; `readOnly: true` blocks all writes; no credentials are ever collected and network operations never prompt (120 s timeout, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`). Details: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md#security-model).

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · Versioning：semver, with `package.json`, the [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) heading and the git tag (`v0.1.0`) always kept in sync. CI runs the test suite on Ubuntu and Windows across Node 22 / 24 — four jobs, all green before a merge.

@yann9/dsh-git-workbench README · Versioning：Pushing a tag *is* the release: `.github/workflows/release.yml` gates on the same matrix, creates the GitHub Release with notes grouped by conventional commit type, and stages the tarball on npm through Trusted Publishing (OIDC — no token in the repository). A staged tarball is not installable until the maintainer approves it with 2FA, so every publish keeps its human check; the workflow checks the packed file list before the tarball leaves the machine. See [docs/development.md](docs/development.md) for the workflow and the Trusted Publisher binding.
